content:
Trig identities feel simple until a paper stacks three at once. Then one wrong sign wipes an easy mark. So take this free JEE Trigonometry DPP online test below. It gives 15 MCQs with instant scoring. Also, every answer carries a short worked step. First aim for 12 out of 15, and log each slip.

What JEE asks from identities

  • Compound and multiple angle formulas, and their quick reversals.
  • Product forms like cos A cos B, so long chains shrink.
  • Conditional identities, because A plus B plus C often equals pi.
  • Ratio values on the unit circle, and their signs by quadrant.
  • Radian measure and arc length, so revision stays complete.

Formulas to revise first

  • First, sin(A + B) spreads to sin A cos B plus cos A sin B.
  • The value sin 2A is 2 sin A cos A, and it saves time.
  • For any triangle, tan A plus tan B plus tan C equals their product.
  • Also, a sin x plus b cos x peaks at root of a squared plus b squared.
  • Arc length is r times theta, so keep theta in radians.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Mixing sin 15 with sin 75, and then flipping the sign.
  • Dividing by cos x, but cos x can be zero there.
  • Squaring an equation, so extra roots sneak in.
  • Forgetting the range on an inverse step, because signs shift.

quiz.title: JEE Trigonometric Identities Online Test
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-level questions across compound angles, product forms, conditional identities, ratios and radian measure. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: JEE Main & Advanced trigonometric ratios and identities

questions.q: 6 radians in degree measure is about (use π = 22/7):
questions.explanation: 6 rad = 6 × (180/π) = 3780/11 = 343 and 7/11 degrees, which is about 343°38′.

questions.q: The range of y = sec²x + cosec²x is:
questions.explanation: The expression equals 4/sin²2x. Since sin²2x peaks at 1, the least value is 4, so the range is [4, ∞).

questions.q: In any triangle ABC, tan A + tan B + tan C equals:
options: tan A tan B tan C
tan A tan B + tan B tan C + tan C tan A
questions.explanation: With A + B + C = π, taking tan on A + B = π − C gives tan A + tan B + tan C = tan A tan B tan C.

questions.q: The value of cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° is:
questions.explanation: Use cos θ cos(60° − θ) cos(60° + θ) = (1/4) cos 3θ with θ = 20°. This gives (1/4) cos 60° = 1/8.

questions.q: Equal arcs subtend 65° and 110° at two circles; the ratio of their radii is:
questions.explanation: Equal arc means r₁θ₁ = r₂θ₂, so r₁/r₂ = θ₂/θ₁ = 110/65 = 22/13.

questions.q: The value of sin 10° sin 50° sin 70° is:
questions.explanation: Use sin θ sin(60° − θ) sin(60° + θ) = (1/4) sin 3θ with θ = 10°. This gives (1/4) sin 30° = 1/8.

questions.q: A wheel makes 360 revolutions per minute; radians turned per second:
questions.explanation: Revolutions per second = 360/60 = 6. Each revolution is 2π radians, so 6 × 2π = 12π.

questions.q: The value of tan 75° − cot 75° is:
questions.explanation: tan 75° = 2 + √3 and cot 75° = 2 − √3. Their difference is 2√3.

questions.q: The period of y = cos 3x is:
questions.explanation: The period of cos bx is 2π/|b|. For b = 3 this equals 2π/3.

questions.q: If sin θ + cos θ = √2, then θ equals:
questions.explanation: sin θ + cos θ = √2 sin(θ + 45°). Its maximum √2 occurs when θ = 45°.

questions.q: A ladder makes an angle with the ground whose sine is 0.8; its foot is 3 m from the wall, so the ladder length is:
questions.explanation: sin θ = 0.8 gives cos θ = 0.6. Since cos θ = base/length, 0.6 = 3/length, so length = 5 m.

questions.q: The domain of f(x) = sec x is:
questions.explanation: sec x = 1/cos x is undefined where cos x = 0, that is at odd multiples of π/2. So the domain is R − (2n + 1)π/2.

questions.q: The range of f(x) = 3 sin 2x − 1 is:
questions.explanation: sin 2x lies in [−1, 1]. Multiply by 3 to get [−3, 3], then subtract 1 to get [−4, 2].

questions.q: cos(A + B) cos(A − B) simplifies to:
questions.explanation: Expand both factors and multiply: (cos A cos B)² − (sin A sin B)² reduces to cos²A − sin²B.

faq.a: Both. It mixes Main-level ratio and identity questions with a few Advanced-style product and range problems, so it stretches you steadily.

faq.q: How should I use these identities on the paper?
faq.a: Name the identity in the first ten seconds, then apply it. Product forms and compound angle rules answer most questions faster than raw expansion.
